one_liner: Senior project/portfolio manager overseeing production schedules, resources, contractors, and metrics for DoD acquisition training courses at Fort Belvoir.
fit_summary: This is a GS-15-equivalent role requiring a bachelor's degree, eight years of portfolio/project management experience, a PMP (or equivalent), and expert IMS/critical-path scheduling skills. Daniel's known strengths are policy knowledge, public engagement, and emergency-management consulting at IEM, but nothing on file shows PMP certification, supervisory experience, or deep scheduling-tool expertise. Unless Daniel's IEM role was heavily project-control focused and long-tenured, this is unlikely to qualify.
eligibility: Open to the public (excepted service, Title 10 §1746); no federal status needed.
Required: PMP certification from PMI or an equivalent project management certification.
Band C requires a bachelor's degree in an appropriate discipline plus at least eight years of experience in the functional area; submit transcripts if education is used to qualify.
Specialized experience must cover multi-project portfolio management, IMS/critical path scheduling, resource forecasting, KPI dashboards, and supervising personnel and contractors.
Security clearance listed as 'Other'; confirm investigation requirements before applying.
strategy: First confirm you hold a PMP or equivalent and eight years of relevant project management experience; if not, don't spend effort here, and instead target GS-9/11 program or emergency management analyst roles where your IEM experience fits.

If applying, describe IEM work strictly in project-control terms: portfolios managed, schedules built, tools used (MS Project, etc.), staff/contractors led, and metrics reported, with dates and hours per week.
Mirror the specialized experience language line by line, since evaluation is pass/fail on minimum qualifications followed by 'best meets mission requirements.'
Keep the resume to two pages: lead with certifications (PMP, any COR or data analytics), then the most relevant positions, stated concisely.
Upload transcripts and the PMP certificate, and submit before November 5, 2026; the window is only two weeks.
resume_bullets: Managed a portfolio of [number] concurrent [emergency management/recovery] projects for [client type], building and maintaining Integrated Master Schedules in [Microsoft Project/tool] with critical path and dependency tracking.
Developed KPI dashboards and executive briefings on schedule adherence, resource utilization, and budget execution for [client leadership level], informing [decision made].
Led a cross-functional team of [number] staff and [number] subcontractors, balancing workload and forecasting resource needs across [number] task orders.
interview_questions: Walk us through how you built and maintained an Integrated Master Schedule for a complex, multi-team portfolio.
Describe a time you identified a critical path risk or resource conflict and what corrective action you recommended.
How have you overseen contractor performance and held teams accountable for deliverables?
Tell us about a briefing you gave to senior executives and how you tailored the data to support a decision.
watch_outs: PMP or equivalent certification is mandatory; without it, the application will likely be screened out.
Senior level (GS-15 equivalent) requiring eight years of specialized experience and supervisory experience that may exceed your background.
Short application window: October 22 to November 5, 2026.
The role is about learning production project controls, not policy or public engagement, so it underuses your strongest skills.
